title: This Bird Flies 44,000 Miles a Year, Pole to Pole and Back

scenes.text: This bird flies from pole to pole and back every year.
Scientists strapped tiny trackers to 60 terns from Greenland.
The birds averaged about 44,000 miles a year.
They flew down to the Weddell Sea near Antarctica and back.
Over a lifetime, that's three trips to the Moon and back.

description:
Arctic terns fly about 44,000 miles a year between Greenland and the Antarctic Weddell Sea.
Over a lifetime that's like three trips to the Moon and back.
Could you handle that commute?
first_comment: Pole to pole every year. What animal journey amazes you most?
